toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% is very likely ordinary week-to-week variation, so I would not roll back. The last 26 weeks average 0.354% with an upper band edge of 0.482%. This week's 0.411% sits inside that band. Three earlier weeks were higher (0.44, 0.47 and 0.51%) and nothing was found when they were investigated. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard count matches a recount from the raw logs. Booking completion didn't change (41.0% to 41.2%), and support logged no complaints.

The "new pods error at twice the rate" figure is a rollout warm-up effect. Every recent rollout shows it, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image. Cold caches cause timeouts, but they add only 10–20 errors per rollout. That can't explain about 2,300 extra errors, and the comparison never matched pods of the same age.

What to do: record the week at ops review as within the normal band. Keep all alerting on, and do not mute it. Apply the standard check to next week. If the week of 2 Nov goes above the band, investigate then. I did not test the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic, so those stay open. Confidence is fairly high.
output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe-style specification of the deviation (is/is-not against 26-week history), then Analysis of Competing Hypotheses on the rollout warm-up vs. release fault vs. normal variation, with an evidence-ledger check of the sources (leadership email and release engineer's note are interpretive; telemetry is independent).
